producer_report.summary: A verifier that hits its deadline is now its own outcome, `VerifierFailure::TimedOut`. It is rerun once on a fresh snapshot, and a second timeout leaves the criteria unjudged. The root cause was that `verification_stage` stored a timeout as the generic `verifier_failure` string. `judge` then failed the verdict on it as it does for a judged failure, so criteria were rejected that nobody had judged. In verify.rs, `VerdictInputs.verifier_failure` is now `Option<VerifierFailure>` with `Incomplete(String)` and `TimedOut(String)`. `TimedOut` gives the reason "the verifier timed out, so the criteria are unjudged: <detail>". Unassessed criteria get 'unjudged' evidence, and there is no 'returned no verdict' reason. `Incomplete` keeps "the verifier did not complete: ..". `pass` still requires no failure. In run/verification.rs a non-Success outcome of `TimedOut` becomes `TimedOut`. Every other failure point becomes `Incomplete`. After the snapshot-unchanged check, a first timeout clears the run's results, rebuilds the snapshot and `continue`s. This shares the two-run cap with the snapshot-fault rerun. The outcome state stays Rejected. display.rs says "the verifier timed out and nothing was judged" instead of "ask again with the findings in mind" for an unjudged result. Tests: three verify.rs unit tests (`a_verifier_that_times_out_is_unjudged_never_a_pass`, `non_timeout_incomplete_failure_keeps_the_did_not_complete_reason`, `non_timeout_failing_check_and_judged_fail_keep_their_reasons`) and three run_pin_tests.rs tests that drive `Athena::go` with a scripted fake verifier (`a_verifier_that_times_out_once_is_rerun_and_the_second_verdict_decides`, `a_verifier_that_times_out_twice_is_unjudged_not_rejected_as_judged`, `non_timeout_verifier_error_is_not_rerun`). They assert the recorded state, reasons, criterion evidence, summary and invocation seq. CHANGELOG.md has a Fixed entry naming the root cause. docs/records.md and docs/design/athena-v0.md (the verification.json row and the 'judges exactly what will land' row) describe the rerun and the unjudged reason.

criteria_check.criterion: The change description names the root cause: a verifier timeout was recorded as the generic `verifier_failure` in crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs and failed the verdict in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs exactly like a judged failure, so criteria were rejected unjudged.
criteria_check.evidence: The CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] Fixed entry and the doc-comment on `VerifierFailure` in verify.rs both state this root cause, naming `verification_stage` in run/verification.rs, `judge` in verify.rs and the generic `verifier_failure` string. Read in the diff.

criteria_check.criterion: A Grep of the diff in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs shows a distinct timeout variant whose reason says 'unjudged' and is separate from 'the verifier did not complete'; it never yields a pass.
criteria_check.evidence: verify.rs defines `VerifierFailure::TimedOut` with the reason `UNJUDGED_REASON_PREFIX` ("the verifier timed out, so the criteria are unjudged"). It is a separate match arm from the `Incomplete` arm, which says "the verifier did not complete". `pass` still requires `verifier_failure.is_none()`. verification.rs builds `TimedOut` when `voutput.outcome == InvocationOutcome::TimedOut`. The test `a_verifier_that_times_out_is_unjudged_never_a_pass` asserts a Fail verdict even when a passing output is supplied.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A new test where the verifier times out on the first run and succeeds on the second ends with the second run's verdict. A second test where it times out twice ends with the unjudged reason, not as a judged rejection. Both fail on the base commit and pass on the change.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core times_out` ran 3 tests, all ok. `a_verifier_that_times_out_once_is_rerun_and_the_second_verdict_decides` asserts runs.len()==2, state Landed, summary "Fine.", empty reasons, and that the recorded verifier invocation is the second run's (first_seq + 1). `a_verifier_that_times_out_twice_is_unjudged_not_rejected_as_judged` asserts runs.len()==2, state Rejected, agent_verdict None, and reasons equal to exactly the unjudged reason. It also asserts every criterion's evidence contains 'unjudged', and that neither the reasons nor finished.reason say 'did not complete'. On the base commit there is no rerun and the reason is 'did not complete', so both fail there. I read this from the base code and did not run them on the base commit.

mistakes: I first wrote the once-timeout pin test against a `finished.invocations` field that does not exist. I replaced it with the seq comparison before the first test run.

learnings: `verification_stage` is a single loop with a `verifier_runs` counter. The snapshot-fault rerun and the new timeout rerun share its cap of 2.

The fake agent driver reports `InvocationOutcome::TimedOut` from a scripted `FakeTurn` (`outcome`, `structured = None`, `detail`), so a timeout can be tested through `Athena::go` without any production seam.
`Finished` carries `verification` but not the invocation list. The pin test checks the second run's seq by comparing it to the seq of the only run of a non-timing-out verifier in the same fixture.
The existing `verifier_failure: None` constructors compile unchanged with the new type, so send_back.rs and the other verify.rs test constructors needed no edit.
